answer: A sybil needs cheap, transferable credibility. Deny it with a pigment that cannot be cloned: each identity's stake is locked per-identity and per-epoch, aged like a rock face. A ridge of minimum staking epochs separates real from clone — a clone must re-lock fresh capital for the full term, so capital cost grows linearly with fleet size. Standing accrues only on a mesa reached by completing the staking term and attested work in the same epoch; skipping the term forfeits the layer. The system verifies lock, attestation, and term on-chain, so a fake identity cannot fake age or share capital.
